[[File:Christian Josef Wiedermann.jpg|thumb|Christian Josef Wiedermann]]
'''Christian J. Wiedermann''' (born 1954 in [[Spittal an der Drau|Molzbichl]], Austria) is an Austrian professor of medicine  in internal medicine, clinical pharmacology, and intensive care. His research includes neuroimmunomodulation, interaction between inflammation and coagulation, fluid therapy in critical care, and ethical concerns in medical research.

== Early life and education ==
Wiedermann earned his medical degree from the [[University of Innsbruck]], where he later specialized in internal medicine, clinical pharmacology, and intensive care medicine. He completed a [[Max Kade]] research fellowship at the [[National Institutes of Health]] in [[Bethesda, Maryland]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Wiedermann |first1=CJ |last2=Adamson |first2=IY |last3=Pert |first3=CB |last4=Bowden |first4=DH |title=Enhanced secretion of immunoreactive bombesin by alveolar macrophages exposed to silica |journal=[[Journal of Leukocyte Biology]] |date=February 1988 |volume=43 |issue=2 |pages=99–103 |doi=10.1002/jlb.43.2.99 |pmid=2826633}}</ref>

== Career ==
Wiedermann has held clinical and academic positions in Austria and Italy. He served as a senior physician at the University Clinic for Internal Medicine in Innsbruck, Austria, and later as head of the Department of Internal Medicine at the Central Hospital in Bolzano, Italy.<ref>[https://news.provinz.bz.it/de/news-archive/73155 Two new department heads at the Bolzano Hospital welcomed by Governor Durnwalder]. In: Presseamt Autonome Provinz Bozen–Südtirol. 23. März 2004. Retrieved 3 April 2025.</ref> He was medical director of Tirol Kliniken,<ref>[https://www.tt.com/artikel/13483724/wiedermann-zweiter-geschaeftsfuehrer-der-tirol-kliniken Wiedermann appointed as second managing director of Tirol Kliniken]. In: Tiroler Tageszeitung, 26. September 2017. Retrieved 3 April 2025.</ref> the regional hospital network in Tyrol, and an associate researcher at the Institute for Public Health, Medical Decision Making, and Health Technology Assessment at the Private University for Health Sciences, Medical Informatics, and Technology in [[Tyrol (state)|Tyrol, Austria]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Institute of Public Health – Publications |url=https://www.umit-tirol.at/page.cfm?vpath=departments/public_health/institute-of-public-health/publications |website=UMIT TIROL – Private University for Health Sciences, Medical Informatics and Technology |language=en |access-date=3 April 2025}}</ref>

He currently coordinates research projects at the Institute of General Practice and Public Health at the Claudiana College of Health Professions in [[Bolzano]], Italy.<ref>{{cite web |title=Prof. Dr. med. univ. Christian Josef Wiedermann |url=https://www.institut-allgemeinmedizin.bz.it/team/ |website=Institute of General Practice South Tyrol |publisher=Institute of General Practice and Public Health Bolzano |language=en |access-date=3 April 2025 |quote=Christian Wiedermann studied medicine at the University of Innsbruck and completed further training in Germany, Italy, and the United States, including at the NIH in Bethesda, Cornell University Medical College, and Harvard Medical School. He held leadership positions at the Medical University of Innsbruck and Bolzano Central Hospital, served as medical director of Tirol Kliniken until 2020, and is a professor of internal medicine at the Medical University of Innsbruck.}}</ref>

== Research and contributions ==
=== Inflammation and intensive care medicine ===
Wiedermann’s early research focused on the interplay between inflammation and neuropeptides, particularly in relation to the immune and nervous system interactions between psychological stress, immune responses, and inflammatory processes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Psyche und Immunsystem |url=https://oe1.orf.at/artikel/213392/Psyche-und-Immunsystem |website=Ö1 – Österreichischer Rundfunk |date=2 November 2008 |access-date=4 April 2025}}</ref>

Building on this foundation, he later examined inflammatory and coagulation pathways in critically ill patients and explored their implications for intravenous [[fluid therapy]]. Wiedermann became a prominent critic of [[hydroxyethyl starch]] (HES), highlighting risks of organ damage. He also contributed to the evaluation of [[albumin]] in sepsis and septic shock. His systematic reviews on HES contributed to growing concerns over tissue storage and kidney injury, which influenced regulatory restrictions for its use in critically ill patients.<ref>{{cite web |title=HES storage in the spotlight |url=https://www.isicem.org/newsletter/1_ISICEM_Tuesday_Final.pdf |website=ISICEM News – Official Newsletter of the International Symposium on Intensive Care and Emergency Medicine |date=18 March 2014 |access-date=4 April 2025 |quote=Christian J. Wiedermann presented an overview of the now controversial use of [[hydroxyethyl starch]] (HES) in patients with hypovolemia, highlighting issues of tissue accumulation and organ damage.}}</ref> He has also contributed to the evaluation of albumin in fluid management for patients with sepsis and septic shock, focusing on potential benefits related to endothelial function and [[oncotic pressure]] in hypoalbuminemic patients.<ref>{{cite web |title=Albumin in Sepsis and Septic Shock |url=https://www.medthority.com/medical-education/albumin-in-fluid-management-learning-zone/albumin-in-sepsis-and-septic-shock/ |website=Medthority |access-date=4 April 2025}}</ref>

=== Bioethics and scientific misconduct ===
Wiedermann has published on ethical questions in clinical guideline development and on the influence of pharmaceutical industry sponsorship. His early work critically assessed the [[Surviving Sepsis Campaign]], including financial conflicts of interest and their potential impact on treatment recommendations.<ref name="Wiedermann2005">{{Cite journal |last=Wiedermann |first=Christian J. |date=July 2005 |title=Bioethics, the Surviving Sepsis Campaign, and the industry |journal=[[Wiener Klinische Wochenschrift]] |volume=117 |issue=13–14 |pages=442–444 |doi=10.1007/s00508-005-0396-x |issn=0043-5325 |pmid=16091869}}</ref> This commentary anticipated and addressed the same issues later raised in a 2006 editorial in the ''New England Journal of Medicine''.<ref name="Eichacker2006">{{Cite journal |last1=Eichacker |first1=Peter Q. |last2=Natanson |first2=Charles |last3=Danner |first3=Robert L. |date=2006-10-19 |title=Surviving Sepsis — Practice Guidelines, Marketing Campaigns, and Eli Lilly |url=https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMp068197 |journal=[[New England Journal of Medicine]] |volume=355 |issue=16 |pages=1640–1642 |doi=10.1056/NEJMp068197 |pmid=17050887 |issn=0028-4793|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Wiedermann contributed to public awareness of scientific misconduct involving German anesthesiologist [[Joachim Boldt]]. He highlighted the implications of fabricated research on HES, which influenced international guidelines for fluid resuscitation. In a 2018 article in ''Science'', Wiedermann was cited for drawing attention to the risks posed by Boldt’s research.<ref name="Marcus2018">{{Cite journal |last=Marcus |first=Adam |date=2018-10-26 |title=A scientist's fraudulent studies put patients at risk |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.362.6413.394-a |journal=Science |volume=362 |issue=6413 |pages=394 |doi=10.1126/science.362.6413.394-a|pmid=30361354 |url-access=subscription }}</ref> He also called for the retraction of Boldt's publications, including those in ''Critical Care Medicine'', based on concerns raised by [[Justus Liebig University Giessen]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bleck |first1=Thomas P. |last2=Buchman |first2=Timothy G. |last3=Chang |first3=Cherylee W. J. |last4=Dellinger |first4=R. Phillip |last5=Deutschman |first5=Clifford S. |last6=Kadri |first6=Sameer S. |last7=Marshall |first7=John C. |last8=Maslove |first8=David M. |last9=Masur |first9=Henry |last10=Osborn |first10=Tiffany M. |last11=Parker |first11=Margaret M. |last12=Rochwerg |first12=Bram |last13=Sarwal |first13=Aarti |last14=Sevransky |first14=Jonathan |last15=Thiagarajan |first15=Ravi R. |date=June 2022 |title=The authors reply |url=https://journals.lww.com/ccmjournal/citation/2022/06000/the_authors_reply.39.aspx |journal=[[Critical Care Medicine]] |language=en-US |volume=50 |issue=6 |pages=e604–e606 |doi=10.1097/CCM.0000000000005529 |pmid=35612454 |issn=1530-0293|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

[[Retraction Watch]] published reports covering the Boldt case and broader concerns about scientific integrity. Wiedermann was acknowledged for drawing early attention to data fabrication and manipulated publications in critical care medicine.<ref>{{cite web |title=Weekend reads: Is science self-correcting? Peer review's emotional burden; retractions at Science |url=https://retractionwatch.com/2018/12/01/weekend-reads-is-science-self-correcting-peer-reviews-undue-emotional-burdens-retractions-at-science/ |website=Retraction Watch |date=1 December 2018 |access-date=4 April 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Weekend reads: A new plagiarism euphemism; how Photoshop abuse destroys science; bias against women authors |url=https://retractionwatch.com/2018/03/10/weekend-reads-a-new-plagiarism-euphemism-how-photoshop-abuse-destroys-science-bias-against-women-authors/ |website=Retraction Watch |date=10 March 2018 |access-date=4 April 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Weekend reads: Manuscript submission headaches; 'trophy generation' goes to grad school; is science f*cked? |url=https://retractionwatch.com/2016/08/13/weekend-reads-manuscript-submission-headaches-trophy-generation-goes-to-grad-school-is-science-fucked/ |website=Retraction Watch |date=13 August 2016 |access-date=4 April 2025}}</ref> An editorial in the ''Journal of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Anesthesia'' credited him as one of the first to inform the journal’s editors about issues with Boldt’s work.<ref name="Rong2025">{{Cite journal |last1=Rong |first1=Lisa Q. |last2=Leshem |first2=Edan |last3=Kaplan |first3=Joel A. |date=2025-02-01 |title=Further Retractions of Dr. Joachim Boldt in the Journal of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Anesthesia |url=https://www.jcvaonline.com/article/S1053-0770(24)00910-8/fulltext |journal=[[Journal of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Anesthesia]] |language=English |volume=39 |issue=2 |pages=360–363 |doi=10.1053/j.jvca.2024.11.016 |issn=1053-0770 |pmid=39648115|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
